Core size: “In general, use the largest core that will fit within the packaging constraints of the application.” End tanks: “Proper manifold shape is critical in minimizing pressure drop and providing uniform flow distribution.” Over-the-top end tanks: “The over-the-top design can starve the top tubes.” Side entry: “ideal for both pressure drop and flow distribution”, though vehicle space usually rules it out. Ducting: “should never be smaller than the radius of the compressor outlet” (Garrett’s example compares areas: a GTX5533R Gen II’s 3.25 in (82.6 mm) outlet, 8.30 in² (53.5 cm²), against 3 in (76.2 mm) ducting, 7.07 in² (45.6 cm²), a restriction). Mounting: air-to-air charge air coolers are typically soft-mounted on rubber isolation grommets, against vibration failure and to allow thermal expansion.

Garrett, “Intercooler Sizing And End Tank Design With Rob Dahm” (2020), https://www.garrettmotion.com/news/newsroom/article/intercooler-sizing-and-end-tank-design-with-rob-dahm/; on this build the hot pipe is smaller than the compressor outlet
Setrab’s suggested oil heat rejection for 450 hp (wet sump; maker guidance), https://www.pegasusautoracing.com/pdfs/SetrabApplicationSuggestions.pdf
